question: How large is seed-to-seed variation of each metric on the 50m baseline?
controls: The 50m baseline corpus (experiments/ladder/50m/data.json) and training configuration at the learning rate the 50m learning-rate record selects, full 50-tokens-per-parameter horizon. Only the training seed changes, set per arm in place of train.json's 42; data order is fixed by the corpus seed.
primary_metric: Standard deviation across seeds of final held-out loss, per source and averaged over sources.
secondary_metrics: The same spread for the pinned early-signal suite (scripts.open_slm_eval: HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, PIQA, ArithMark) on each seed's final export, and for held-out loss at each quarter of the horizon.
decision_rule: No decision. The per-metric standard deviation sets the rung's minimum detectable effect: a later 50m contrast reports an effect on a metric only when the difference between arms exceeds 2.83 times that standard deviation, two standard deviations of a difference between two independent runs. Arms that share initial tensors can only be less noisy, so the rule is conservative.
cost: Local RTX 3090 at its synthetic compiled rate of 100,000 tokens per second, before validation and saves: about 7.3 hours per seed, no grant GPU-hours.
